findings.title: CLAIM_EXIT's rewritten third alternative silently stops matching real, unchanged exit-contract prose
locations: docs/src/guide/verbs.md:7 (unaffected by this diff, now silently un-flagged)
findings.why_it_matters: The stated purpose of the third alternative is to catch this package's own phrasing of the exit contract so a checklist item forces someone to verify it — the whole mechanism exists because src/GBGCodingTools.jl's 'the exit contract is 0 clean, 1 substantive finding...' line once contributed ZERO checklist items and a seeded mutation there went undetected. Fixing a real false positive (a digit that is part of a version number, e.g. 'v1.0.0' or '2.5') by adding (?<![\w.]) is correct on its own, but the third alternative was ALSO given a new trailing requirement, \s+[a-z] right after the digit, that the first two alternatives do not need and that has nothing to do with excluding decimal numbers. That extra requirement fails whenever a real exit-code claim wraps its digit in backticks or bold markup and the describing word is not on the very same textual span — which is exactly how this package's own generated guide page phrases it: docs/src/guide/verbs.md line 7 reads '...The exit contract is one for all: `0`' with 'clean,' only appearing on line 8. Verified empirically in a live Julia session: occursin(OLD, line7) == true, occursin(NEW, line7) == false. docs/src/guide/verbs.md is untouched by this diff and lives under docs/src, one of the four SOURCE_SURFACES every check-docs/check-consistency/audit-changes round's claim checklist reads, so every future round over this file silently loses this checklist item with no warning — the same class of unpaid debt the mechanism was built to close, reopened by the very patch meant to sharpen it. IMPLEMENTATION.md's identically-shaped 'Exit contract (every verb): **0** clean · **1** ... · **2** ...' line regresses the same way (OLD true, NEW false).
findings.description: The fix widened its guard beyond the defect it targeted: excluding a digit that continues into a decimal (the actual false-positive class, e.g. 'v1.0.0', '2.5') only requires a check on what follows the digit (mirrored correctly by the first two alternatives via (?!\.\d)), not a requirement that the digit be immediately followed by whitespace-then-a-lowercase-word. The added \s+[a-z] suffix is unrelated to the stated defect and introduces a new, undisclosed false-negative class: any backtick- or bold-wrapped digit whose describing word sits elsewhere (a markdown line break, punctuation, or a closing '**'/'`' immediately after the digit) is now invisible to the checklist, even though the OLD regex — and a same-line integration test would have shown — correctly caught it. No new test in this diff exercises a backtick- or bold-wrapped exit-code claim, so the regression shipped unnoticed.
findings.evidence: docs/src/guide/verbs.md:6-9 (current file, unmodified by this diff): "...so the page cannot drift from the code. The exit contract is one for all: `0`\nclean, `1` a substantive finding (the gate's refusal over an open round is one), `2` cannot evaluate (a\nprecondition not met, missing input, torn file), `3` crash." — line 7 alone (as claim_checklist reads it, one readlines() line at a time) contains "exit contract" and "`0`" but no letter after the digit on that line. Live check: `julia -e 'OLD=r"..."i; NEW=r"..."i; println(occursin(OLD,l)," ",occursin(NEW,l))'` on that exact line printed `true false`.

findings.title: CLAIM_TOOL_ID's `gbg <verb>` alternative now requires a literal backtick, narrower than the disclosed rationale
findings.why_it_matters: The commit-adjacent comment motivates the CLAIM_QUANTIFIER/CLAUSE change purely as 'same clause as a register id or a backticked gbg verb' — a co-occurrence fix — but the tool-id half itself was independently narrowed from any word-bounded 'gbg <verb>' mention to only a backtick-prefixed one, dropping the trailing \b too. A corpus sweep (this repo's own .jl/.md/.toml/.json/.js files, .gbg/ excluded) found 3 lines where a quantifier and a bare (non-backticked) 'gbg <verb>' mention share one clause under the old rule but no longer co-occur under the new one purely because of the backtick requirement (independent of the intentionally-dropped all/any/only words and of the clause split, which account for the other ~536 changed lines and are the disclosed, intended part of this narrowing). This silently drops a small number of real quantifier claims about the tool from the checklist.
findings.description: Distinct from the CLAIM_EXIT finding: here the observed effect is small (3 lines in the current corpus) and plausibly intentional collateral of tightening CLAIM_TOOL_ID to 'the tool is quoted as code' (backticked) rather than 'the word gbg appears', which is a defensible tightening on its own — but it is not the change the surrounding comment claims to be making (a same-clause requirement), so a reader auditing the comment against the code would not expect this second, independent narrowing.
findings.evidence: Corpus script comparing occursin(NEW_Q, clause) && occursin(OLD_ID_no_backtick, clause) against occursin(NEW_Q, clause) && occursin(NEW_ID_with_backtick, clause) over the same per-clause split found 3 lines true under the former and false under the latter, e.g. IMPLEMENTATION.md:280 '`gbg self verify` | recomputes the running copy's git tree hash ... run by every `round` verb and by `gate`' loses its match only when the backtick requirement is added on top of the clause split.
